clue.text: One involved in distribution of credits on courses

indicators.note: to be involved in something is to be caught up inside it, so the single letter sits within the other letters
a distribution spreads things out in a new order, so the letters that follow are dealt out afresh

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A university registrar handing out academic credits for the modules students have taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A course is a route or heading someone takes, and directions are the routes travelled.

clue.text: Johnson & Johnson?

parts.note: surface reading: the healthcare products company with the doubled surname
setter's reading: one Johnson is Boris, who sat in the Commons as an elected MP; the other is slang for the male organ, which has a coy euphemism of the same word

explanation.walkthrough: Each Johnson is read differently: one is the former UK Prime Minister who sat in Parliament, the other is American slang for the male organ.
explanation.definitionFit: An MP is a Member of Parliament, and the same word is a coy euphemism for the penis, which slang also calls a johnson.

clue.text: Hoskins would start to examine answer to make clue

parts.note: Hoskins is the setter, who would say I'd

indicators.note: the start of the following word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

parts.note: opening letter of examine
A is the standard abbreviation for answer

explanation.surface: The setter describes how he would go about writing a crossword clue.
explanation.walkthrough: A setter often refers to himself by pseudonym, so Hoskins stands for I or me; here 'Hoskins would' becomes I'D.
explanation.definitionFit: As in 'I haven't a clue', a clue here means a notion or inkling of something.

clue.text: Goods for those possibly full of gas?

parts.note: pro means in favour of
pipes or channels that may carry gas

explanation.surface: A question about which goods are suited to people who are full of hot air.
explanation.definitionFit: Products are manufactured items offered for sale, which is what goods means in commerce.

clue.text: Mountainous island fit for climbing

indicators.note: in a down clue, climbing means reading upward, so the word is taken bottom to top

parts.note: fit as in capable

explanation.surface: Describes a hilly island suited to hikers and climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Elba is a hilly Mediterranean isle off Tuscany, where Napoleon was exiled.

clue.text: Salary? Mine must be returned in post!

indicators.note: in places the reversed word inside the word for post

parts.note: to post a letter is to send it

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so this word is written backwards

parts.note: a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A miner's demand that his wages be sent back to him in the mail.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular payment, especially to a clergyman, so it is a kind of salary.

clue.text: In the morning, grunts lifting up letter

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up raises the bottom letters to the top, so the whole is read upward

parts.note: a.m. means before noon
grunt is US slang for an infantry soldier, a GI

explanation.surface: Soldiers groaning as they lift something heavy first thing in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: Sigma is the eighteenth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter.

clue.text: Embarrassed around naked milf (also hot under collar)

indicators.note: around puts the colour word on both sides of the stripped word

parts.note: someone embarrassed goes red in the face

indicators.note: naked means stripped of its covering, so the outside letters are removed and only the inner part stays

parts.note: the inner two letters of milf

explanation.surface: A racy scene in which someone blushes at an unclothed older woman and gets flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: The brackets are part of the clue: 'also' is a link word and the definition is 'hot under collar'.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot under the collar is an idiom for angry and irritated, which is what being riled means.

clue.text: Unpleasant type poking face using fingers

indicators.note: something poking into another thing pushes itself inside it

parts.note: dial is slang for a person's face
git is British slang for a contemptible person

explanation.surface: A nasty person jabbing someone in the face with their fingers.
explanation.walkthrough: Both GIT and DIAL are British slang: a git is an annoying person, and a dial is a face.
explanation.definitionFit: Digital literally means relating to the fingers or digits, and a digit is a finger.

clue.text: Large parts I flipping look at lustily

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the result is read back to front
a thing that parts another splits it and sits in the gap

parts.note: ego is Latin for I, and the self
L is the size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Someone admits staring lecherously at another person's large body parts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' looks like a mild British swear word; here it reverses the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: To ogle is to stare at someone with obvious sexual interest.

clue.text: German dons drunk brandy with ale mostly

indicators.note: to don is to put on clothing, so the abbreviation wraps itself around the letters
drunk words are unsteady and fall into a jumbled order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: German academics at a college getting drunk on brandy, mostly with beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like it shortens the ale, but it is the definition; 'with' just joins the two drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: By and large is an idiom meaning on the whole or in general, which is what mostly means.

clue.text: Worker in a chippy, one with a violent past?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: someone who coats fish in batter; a chippy is a British fish and chip shop
second meaning: someone who has beaten another person

explanation.walkthrough: A chippy is a British fish and chip shop, though it can also mean a carpenter, which sends solvers the wrong way.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both someone who dips food in batter and a person who has repeatedly beaten someone.

clue.text: Where the man in pub is turned around?

definitions.text: Where the man in pub is turned around?

indicators.note: in puts the pronoun inside the word for pub
turned around means facing the other way, so the combined letters are read backwards

parts.note: first part of BAR, a pub
he is the pronoun for a man
last letter of BAR, a pub

explanation.surface: A drinker in a pub who decides to change his ways.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a rehab clinic is where a heavy drinker turns his life around.
explanation.definitionFit: Rehab is short for rehabilitation, treatment where people recovering from addiction get their lives back on track.

clue.text: Pure heroin snorted by actors with MDMA

indicators.note: a drug that is snorted is taken in, so the letter goes inside the word for actors

parts.note: first part of CAST, the actors in a play
H is slang for heroin
rest of CAST
E is slang for ecstasy, the drug MDMA

explanation.surface: A drug scandal in which actors snort heroin and take ecstasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the cast taking hard drugs is anything but pure.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means virtuous and sexually abstinent, so morally pure.

clue.text: Possible a vile beach needs to be sorted out

indicators.note: sorting out means rearranging things, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A filthy beach could be cleaned up, given the effort.
explanation.definitionFit: Something achievable can be accomplished, which means it is within the bounds of the possible.

clue.text: Laugh about Phil's missus being an illustrious type

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the laugh wraps around the other piece

parts.note: ho is a laugh, as in ho ho
Prince Philip's wife was Queen Elizabeth, ER

explanation.surface: Someone chuckles about Phil's wife being a famous person.
explanation.walkthrough: Phil is Prince Philip, whose missus (wife) was Queen Elizabeth II, signed ER for Elizabeth Regina.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is someone admired and celebrated for great deeds, an illustrious figure.

clue.text: I react excitedly, having screened old smut

indicators.note: to screen is to shield or enclose, so the jumbled letters surround the abbreviation
something done excitedly is agitated and disorderly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: Someone getting worked up after watching an old dirty film.
explanation.definitionFit: Erotica is sexually explicit literature or art, which is what smut means.

clue.text: A red swelling initially hurts

parts.note: taken as written
Che Guevara was a famous communist, a red

indicators.note: initially points to the beginning of the word before it, so only its opening letter counts

parts.note: opening letter of swelling

explanation.surface: A red, swollen patch that is painful to touch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Red' wants to be a colour describing the swelling; here it is a communist, Che Guevara.
explanation.definitionFit: To ache is to feel a dull continuous pain, so a body part that aches hurts.

clue.text: Fine everybody that's conservative

parts.note: everybody means all people
conservatives are on the political right

explanation.surface: Someone declares they are happy with everybody being conservative.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something is all right means it is acceptable or satisfactory, a common sense of fine.

clue.text: Stop royal ultimately entering Balmoral?

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the letter is put within the other word

parts.note: first part of HAT; a Balmoral is a Scottish flat bonnet

indicators.note: ultimately means at the very end, so only the final letter of the preceding word is used

parts.note: final letter of royal
end of HAT

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a royal from getting into Balmoral Castle, the royal family's Scottish estate.
explanation.walkthrough: Balmoral wants to be the royal castle; here it is a Scottish brimless cap, so a hat, as the question mark warns.
explanation.definitionFit: Halt is a verb and noun for stopping or coming to a standstill.

clue.text: Small piece of gum or Sellotape

indicators.note: of here means taken from within, so the letters come out of the run of words that follows

parts.note: spans the end of gum, all of or and the start of Sellotape

explanation.surface: A tiny bit of chewing gum or sticky tape; Sellotape is the British brand name for clear adhesive tape.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a small mouthful or fragment of something, especially food.

clue.text: Solo male part rejected by composer

parts.note: Johann Sebastian Bach, the composer

indicators.note: something rejected is sent back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: a part in a play is a role

explanation.surface: A composer turns down a solo part written for a male singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bachelor is a man who has never married, so he is a single, unattached man.

clue.text: Two firms working to make a case?

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, and two of them
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: Two companies cooperating to build a legal case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' suggests a lawsuit, but it is the silk casing a caterpillar spins.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocoon is the silky protective covering spun by a larva, an enclosing case.

clue.text: Love and marriage, don't start that as it can make you cry!

indicators.note: telling a word not to start means dropping its opening letter

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, which looks like O
a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: A cynic warning someone not to bring up love and marriage, since it only ends in tears.
explanation.definitionFit: Chopping this vegetable releases a compound that irritates the eyes and makes them water.

clue.text: This ironic broadcast is overly dramatic

indicators.note: broadcast seed is scattered widely, so the letters land in a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A critic complains that a sarcastic TV or radio programme is melodramatic.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is theatrical and exaggerated, as in hamming it up for attention.

clue.text: Chat volubly after drop of Tanqueray gin?

indicators.note: after places the chatter's word behind the single letter
a drop is a tiny amount, so only the first letter of the brand is taken

parts.note: opening letter of Tanqueray, a brand of gin
to rap is to talk at length, or to chat

explanation.surface: Someone becomes chatty after a sip of Tanqueray, a well-known brand of gin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gin' looks like the drink, but a gin is also a snare for catching animals, as the question mark hints.
explanation.definitionFit: A gin, short for engine, is an old word for a snare or device for catching animals.

clue.text: Lad that's served up hot food

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means brought upward, so the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot on taps
a son is a lad

explanation.surface: A boy who has been dished up something warm to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosh is British slang for food, a meal or grub.

clue.text: Bitter Conservative needs help all around

indicators.note: all around means on every side, so the second word encloses the first

parts.note: start of AID, help
C is the abbreviation for Conservative
rest of AID

explanation.surface: A resentful Tory politician who needs support from everyone.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid describes a sharp, sour taste or a cutting tone, both senses of bitter.

clue.text: Party led by adulterous leader? For shame!

indicators.note: led by puts the selected letter in front of the word for party
the leader of a word is its first letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of adulterous
a bash is a party

explanation.surface: A political party headed by a cheating leader, met with cries of disgrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For shame!' reads as an exclamation, but 'For' is a link word and the definition is the verb 'shame'.
explanation.definitionFit: To abash is to make someone feel embarrassed and humiliated, so to shame them.

clue.text: Bit of lolly found in hot cake

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so the letter goes within the word for hot

parts.note: start of STOLEN; hot is slang for stolen goods

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a small part of it, here its first letter

parts.note: opening letter of lolly
end of STOLEN

explanation.surface: Some money, lolly being British slang for cash, discovered inside a cake fresh from the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hot' suggests a warm cake; it means stolen, as with hot goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Stollen is a rich German fruit loaf with marzipan, traditionally eaten at Christmas.
